chunks: Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Muhammad ibn al-Husayn, and a number of our companions, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Khalid, altogether from Uthman ibn Isa, from Sama'ah ibn Mihran, who said:

I asked him (peace be upon him) about a man who has a wife and a concubine, and it becomes inevitable for him to emancipate his concubine and marry her. He (peace be upon him) said: If he wishes, he stipulates upon her that her emancipation is her dower, for that is permissible; or he stipulates upon her, if he wishes, he divides (his time) for her, and if he wishes he does not divide; and if he wishes he prefers the free woman over her. So if she is pleased with that, there is no problem.

key_terms.حُرَّةٌ: Free woman (as opposed to a slave)

ai.seo_question: What are the permissible stipulations when a man emancipates his concubine and marries her?
ai.summary: In this ruling from *Al-Kafi*, Imam al-Sadiq (AS) addresses the legal flexibility in manumitting a slave concubine (*surriyya*) and marrying her, establishing that her freedom can serve as her dower (*mahr*) or be accompanied by specific marital conditions. This highlights the Shia juristic view that such arrangements are permissible provided the woman consents to terms regarding time division or preference over a free wife, reflecting the practical social dynamics of the era. The hadith underscores the contractual nature of these unions, allowing for negotiated terms that balance the rights of the woman with the man's discretion.

en.hubeali: Muhammad Bin Yahya, from Muhammad Bin Al Husayn, and a number of our companions, from Ahmad Bin Muhammad Bin Khalid, altogether from Usman Bin Isa, from Sama’at Bin Mihran who said,

‘I asked him<sup>asws</sup> about a man who had a wife for him, and a concubine. It became inevitable for him that he emancipates his concubine, and marries her’. So he<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘If he so desires to, he stipulates upon her that her emancipation would be her dower, for that is Permissible; or he stipulates upon her, if he so desires to, he divides (his time) for her, and if he so desires to he does not divide (his time for her); and if he so desires to he prefers the free woman over her. So if she is pleased with that, so there is no problem’.
